quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees the other driver will yield to you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee the other driver will yield to you.
It tells the other driver you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the other driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means another driver will yield to you. Do not depend on it for your safety.

questions.question: If you are riding behind a car, where should you position yourself?

options.text: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
Always stay on the far left side of the lane.
Do not worry about your position.
Always stay on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when behind a car. The driver will see you best in their rearview mirror from this position. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When passing on a motorcycle, what is different from passing in a car?

options.text: Being seen is more important on a motorcycle.
Being seen is less important on a motorcycle.
Always pass on the shoulder instead of the road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being seen is more important on a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. You can easily hide in a car's blind spot. Drivers may not notice you even if looking your way. Being visible is very important.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?

options.text: Yellow with black letters or symbols
Blue with white letters or symbols
White with black letters or symbols
White with red borders

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black letters or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert you to dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What can happen if you brake too hard?

options.text: Your wheels may lose traction and skid.
You will stop sooner than expected.
Your tire may pop.
You will take longer to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels may lose traction and skid.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard causes your wheels to lose grip on the road. This can cause your motorcycle to skid and crash.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Ride more slowly than usual.
Slow down later than usual.
Squeeze into small gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Your motorcycle will speed up slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride slowly, slow down early, keep more space between vehicles, and wait for larger gaps before entering traffic.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Speed up.
Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let a tailgater pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster and increase danger. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers will not expect you there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: When does alcohol impair your riding ability?

options.text: Well before the legal limit.
Once you reach the legal limit.
Just above the legal limit.
Well above the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Well before the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Impairment begins well before you reach the legal limit.

questions.question: How do you know if a motorcycle fits you properly?

options.text: You can touch the ground with your feet while seated.
The seat is level with your waist.
The seat is 10 inches above your waist.
The seat is 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch the ground with your feet while seated.
questions.explanation: A proper fit allows your feet to touch the ground while you sit on the seat. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is illegal.
It is slowing down by turning off the engine.
It is slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
It damages the engine and should be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Engine braking is shifting down to a lower gear to slow your motorcycle. It works like applying the brakes.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in a single-file formation.
Ride in a side-by-side formation.
Use both lanes if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups should ride in a single-file formation through curves, turns, when entering or leaving highways. Staggered formation is used on straight roads.

questions.question: Several factors affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Which one does NOT affect it?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast a person drinks
Body weight
Height

questions.correctAnswerText: Height
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In the front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.
Beside the lead rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This keeps them from falling behind and allows experienced riders to watch them.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Only take a few minutes.
Take more than an hour.
Be complicated to perform.
Not be done before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only take a few minutes.
questions.explanation: You should inspect your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Which of the following will protect your eyes from the wind?

options.text: Goggles
Windshield
Sunglasses
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, sunglasses, and eyeglasses do not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: A helmet will NOT provide the best protection if it:

options.text: Is certified by the DOT.
Fits snugly.
Is free of defects.
Has cracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has cracks.
questions.explanation: A helmet should be DOT certified, fit snugly, and be free of damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps to provide maximum protection.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Less frequent attention than a car.
More frequent attention than a car.
To have pre-ride checks performed only by a mechanic.
To be serviced only at a dealer.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent attention than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should consider:

options.text: Whether or not other drivers will see you.
How many cars are on the road ahead.
Which portion of the lane will result in a shorter trip.
If you can pass more vehicles in a certain position than in another.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether or not other drivers will see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers and gives you enough space to react safely.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite of the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle as that can be unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At faster speeds, motorcycles must lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn to lean the motorcycle correctly.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:

options.text: Your right hand.
Your right foot.
Your left hand.
Your left foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: On a motorcycle, the gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal your intentions, as that may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing. Signal first. Check for oncoming traffic. Pass only when it is safe. Then signal again and return to your original lane.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:

options.text: Far from home.
On short trips.
On long rides.
Several hours into the ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles. They occur just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Always use both brakes.
Only use the front brake.
Only use the rear brake on slippery surfaces, such as wet pavement.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This applies to all road conditions.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Involve riders who have operated their motorcycles for less than six months.
Are caused by faulty ignition systems.
Occur because of distractions caused by passengers.
Happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders who have operated their motorcycles for less than six months.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle. Be extra careful when riding an unfamiliar bike.
